verdict.rationale: Bento's own marketing and FAQ copy says it scores every release against production history (offline, in CI and on live traffic) to catch regressions. It also says prompt, skill and model changes are versioned and diffable, with drift over prompt versions shown out of the box. However, no evidence describes a side-by-side comparison view of eval runs, and the claims are high-level marketing statements. Missing for 10: a documented side-by-side eval-run comparison UI or CLI, eval-dataset run definitions, per-metric diff detail, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can compare eval runs side by side to catch regressions between prompt or model versions

citations.quote: Every release scored against your production history — offline, in CI, and on live traffic. Catches regressions before users do.
Every prompt, skill, and model change is versioned, diffable, and reversible. Trace any regression back to the change that caused it.
drift over prompt versions, and regressions across deploys out of the box
